To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the newly developed pyridines 8, 9, 15-19, and 21 displayed selective growth inhibition of the breast MCF-7 cell line, with a marginal effect on the normal Hs27 cell lines, and showed a remarkable antioxidant potential in the DPPH assay.
two novel pyridine derivatives 8, 19, 16, 17 and 15 were identified as promising anticancer and antioxidant agents with moderate to weak PGE3A inhibitory potential.

the newly developed compounds displayed selective in vitro growth inhibition of the breast MCF-7 cancer cell line with no significant effect on the normal human foreskins fibroblast HSF-27 cell line, in addition, the compounds showed moderate to weak in vitro PDE3A inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a series of novel pyridines, and the evaluation of their in vitro anticancer potential against the breast (MCF7), hepatocellular (Hep-G2) and colon (CACO-2) cancer cells.

the design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and in silico ADME-T study of two series of novel polyfunctional pyridines as anticancer and antioxidant agents, with a special focus on the PDE3A inhibition.
the development of a novel series of alkoxylated pyridines with potential anticancer and antioxidant activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

compounds 8, and 19 are the most promising compounds in this study, with a good anticancer potential against breast cancer cell line MCF7, with a high antioxidant potential, low toxicity, and a good predicted bioavailability and drug-likeness.
compounds 8, and 16-19, especially 8 and 16, represent novel anticancer agents with a high potential for further development.
the newly synthesized compounds are potential anticancer and antioxidant agents, which could be further explored as PDE3A inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the newly designed and synthesized pyridine derivatives are promising anticancer candidates, which may be further developed for the treatment of breast cancer.
the synthesized pyridines could be considered as promising anticancer and antioxidant agents, and as potential PDE3A inhibitors.
the novel synthesized compounds are potential candidates for future in vivo anticancer evaluation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the newly developed compounds are worthy of further in-depth investigation as potential anticancer agents.
compounds 8, and 15-19 may be considered as promising anticancer leads with antioxidant potential.
these novel compounds are promising anticancer and antioxidant agents with good ADME properties.
